forecast-period.text: A low pressure trough in the north and east is slowly moving east. Another trough in the southeast with a low pressure system developing near the Victorian border during today will also move further east. In the west, a high pressure system will move into the Bight and slowly move east to be centred over Victoria on Monday, while extending a ridge into parts of the state. Another trough near the WA border is expected to develop from Saturday and extend into the state before weakening by Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible morning fog about the west coast and Eyre Peninsula. Isolated showers about the southeast, clearing during the evening. Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing over the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh about the southeast coast.
Isolated showers about the southeast. Isolated thunderstorms are possible about the eastern districts and parts of the far northwest. Southeast to southwesterly winds.
Isolated showers and thunderstorms over the far west, extending into central parts during the day. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to northeasterly winds.
Possible morning fog in the far west. Mostly dry, though a slight chance of an isolated shower or thunderstorm over the far north. Maximum temperatures below average. Light winds.

text.p: Showers about the agricultural areas, clearing during the day. Maximum temperatures below average. Northwesterly winds in the south, tending south to southwesterly during the day. South to southeasterly winds in the north.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: Less than 2 mm across the far northeast. 2 to 10 mm elsewhere, increasing to 10 to 20 mm in the northwest with isolated falls reaching up to 40 mm.
